title: Hold a fallen trailer tongue up while rolling the heavy rover back under it, then lower it onto the ball
instruction: Hitch the trailer to the rover.
context: Hitching a trailer whose tongue rests on the ground takes two hands at once: one carries the tongue at the ball's height, the other brings the vehicle under it, and the tongue is lowered, not dropped, onto the ball. Neither body can be carried to the other: the trailer is chocked and its tongue falls when let go; the 14 kg rover rolls but cannot be lifted. Backed up with the tongue down, the rover passes over the socket. Unlike lifting a load and sliding a support under it (#133, #338, #830), the body brought under is a rolling vehicle that must stop a few millimetres short, since the socket swings toward it as it is lowered, and the seat is a cup on a ball; unlike #1090, the coupler does not wait at its height; unlike #1594 (a falling forearm held level while a pin is pushed in), the part brought is a rolling 14 kg vehicle.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Track: an earth-brown sheet of painted PVC foil 4 mm thick, x 14 to 46, y -42 to 52. Trailer: a two-wheeled trailer, 9 kg in all: a painted aluminium bed 13 x 16 cm with its load: a lead block 12 x 7 x 7.2 cm (6.8 kg) bolted across the bed's front, from 5 cm ahead of the axle to 2 cm behind it (its centre 1.5 cm ahead), and a box 10 x 10 x 6 cm of empty sheet steel on the bed, its wheels' axle at y 36.0 (x 30 between them), wheels 7 cm across, track 16 cm; its centre of mass 1.2 cm ahead of the axle, so the tongue's tip bears about 5 N; the tongue (1.6 x 1.4 cm aluminium bar) runs from 2 cm behind the axle 20 cm forward (-y) to a socket at its tip: a square steel cup 2.6 cm across inside, 1.2 cm deep, open downward, resting on the ground at (30, 16.2). Four yellow chocks 3 x 3 x 2.5 cm screwed to the track against the trailer's wheels, fore and aft. Rover: built heavy at the size of a 1:18 trail crawler (Traxxas TRX-4M body shell, painted yellow, white roof), 26.2 x 12.4 x 11.7 cm, lead-filled, 14 kg in all, centre of mass 5.5 cm up; free-rolling wheels, front pair crowned, turntable front axle with its steering straight and held by friction; its origin at (30, -13.0), facing -y (its back to the trailer). Tow tabs: dark grey 3D-printed PLA tabs 5.0 x 1.6 x 1.6 cm on each bumper, 4.5 cm up. Tow ball: a steel ball 1.6 cm across on a 2.2 cm post on the rear tab, its centre 8.8 cm up (8.4 cm above the track) at (30, 4.2), 12 cm short of the socket.
scoring: 0 if at any time the tongue falls onto the ball: either its socket (while its rim is less than 15 cm above the ball's top, or below it, and its centre, the middle of its opening at its rim's height, within 2.6 cm of the ball's centre horizontally) or its bar's underside straight above the ball (while the ball is under the bar and that point less than 15 cm above the ball's top) falls more than 4 mm over 3 control steps (0.15 s) at a peak speed over 0.08 m/s (its sampled speed, or one step's fall over 0.05 s) (the tongue dropped onto the ball), or both tyres of a rover axle are more than 1 cm off the ground for 0.5 s. Otherwise, at the end, after 2 s with the rover and the trailer at rest (under 5 mm/s, the trailer turning under 0.05 rad/s) and released (no point of either gripper, and no point along either arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the rover, its wheels and steering, or the trailer's body): 1.0 if the socket is seated on the ball (the ball's centre within 7.5 mm of the socket's centre horizontally, inside the square cup, and the socket's rim 0 to 6 mm below the ball's centre, its cap resting on the ball); 0.5 if the ball's centre is within 1 cm of the socket's centre (the middle of its opening, at its rim's height) but it is not seated; 0 otherwise. A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lower the tongue onto the ground, chock the trailer's wheels and set the rover on its marks 12 cm ahead of the socket.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The rover is 14 kg (an arm cannot lift an axle), with free wheels and drag; the trailer's wheels are free but chocked (the chocks are fixed); its centre of mass is set 1.2 cm ahead of its axle. The socket is a cup of boxes over a sphere: no latch is modelled; the tongue's weight keeps it seated. Friction: tyres 1.0, track 0.8, socket 0.5, ball 0.4, tongue 0.8.
